questions.question: According to the 'Open- vs. Closed-Weight LLMs' slide, which of the following is a characteristic of Open-Weight models?
options: A. They are higher performing frontier models.
B. They are free to download and can be run locally.
C. They have variable costs and credit allowances.
D. They are easier to use/deploy via interfaces.

questions.question: Which of the following is cited as an example of a fully open model in the 'Training Data' section?
options: A. Claude
B. Gemini
C. Olmo from Ai2
D. The New York Times Company

questions.question: What tradeoffs should be considered when evaluating model size and intelligence?
options: A. Speed vs. Accuracy vs. Cost vs. Privacy
B. Size vs. Knowledge vs. Performance vs. Cost
C. Open vs. Closed vs. Local vs. Cloud
D. Input vs. Output vs. Context vs. Tokens

questions.question: How is 'context' defined in the context of LLMs?
options: A. The total number of parameters in the model.
B. How much text (or other information) a model can access while generating subsequent tokens.
C. The cost per task for using the model.
D. The specific programming language the model is trained on.

questions.question: Which of the following is listed as a benchmark evaluation tool for LLMs?
options: A. SWE-Bench Pro
B. GitHub Copilot
C. Hugging Face
D. NVIDIA Nemotron
